message.content:
Below is a **gcloud CLI** command that will create a Compute Engine instance on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
(If you prefer the REST API, let me know and I’ll provide the equivalent JSON payload.)

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set your project and zone
PROJECT_ID="your-project-id"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2️⃣  Create a new instance with an RTX A6000 GPU
gcloud compute instances create "rtx-a6000-ubuntu" \
  --project="${PROJECT_ID}" \
  --zone="${ZONE}" \
  --machine-type="n1-standard-8" \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
  --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \         # Ubuntu 20.04 LTS
  --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
  --boot-disk-size="100GB" \                 # Size of the boot disk
  --boot-disk-type="pd-ssd" \                # SSD boot disk
  --maintenance-policy="TERMINATE" \         # Terminate on host maintenance
  --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1" \  # 1 RTX A6000 GPU
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # Optional: custom startup script
  --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform" \  # Full access
  --tags="http-server,https-server" \        # Allow HTTP/HTTPS traffic
  --network-tier="PREMIUM" \                 # Premium network tier
  --reservation-affinity="any" \             # No reservation
  --no-creation-error-checks \               # Skip creation error checks
  --quiet                                      # Suppress prompts
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--project` | Your GCP project ID |
| `--zone` | Compute Engine zone (e.g., `us-central1-a`) |
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration (`n1-standard-8` is a good starting point) |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | Disk size & type |
| `--maintenance-policy` | How to handle host maintenance (`TERMINATE` will stop the instance) |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the RTX A6000 GPU (`count=1` for a single GPU) |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: run a shell script on first boot |
| `--scopes` | OAuth scopes for the instance (full access here) |
| `--tags` | Network tags for firewall rules (HTTP/HTTPS) |
| `--network-tier` | Premium network tier for lower latency |
| `--reservation-affinity` | Use any available reservation |
| `--no-creation-error-checks` | Skip creation error checks (useful for scripts) |
| `--quiet` | Suppress interactive prompts |

### Optional: Startup Script

If you want to install CUDA, cuDNN, or other GPU drivers automatically, create a `startup.sh` file:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install NVIDIA drivers and CUDA
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
sudo reboot
```

Then reference it with `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh`.

---

#### REST API Alternative

If you’d rather use the REST API directly, the equivalent JSON payload would look like this:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/your-project-id/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "tags": { "items": ["http-server", "https-server"] },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nsudo reboot"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Send this payload to the Compute Engine Instances insert endpoint:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/your-project-id/zones/us-central1-a/instances
```

Make sure you have the proper OAuth token (`scope=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/compute`) and replace `your-project-id` with your actual project ID.

Let me know if you’d like help with authentication, setting up the REST call, or anything else!
